'''Yan Xiyun''' ({{Lang-zh|阎锡蕴}}; born February 1957) is a Chinese [[nanobiotechnology|nanobiologist]], academician of the [[Chinese Academy of Sciences]], researcher and doctoral supervisor of the [[Institute of Biophysics, Chinese Academy of Sciences|Institute of Biophysics]], and professor of the [[University of the Chinese Academy of Sciences]]. Her main accomplishment was the discovery of [[Artificial enzyme#Nanozymes|nanozymes]] and its application in [[tumor]] diagnosis.<ref name="springer"> {{cite web |last1=Duan |first1=D |last2=Fan |first2=K |last3=Zhang |first3=D |last4=Tan |first4=S |last5=Liang |first5=M |last6=Liu |first6=Y |title=Profile of Xiyun Yang |url=https://link.springer.com |website=Springer Link}}</ref>

== Early life and career ==
Xiyun Yan attended [[Zhengzhou University|Henan Medical University]] and obtained her B.S. degree in 1983. Following that, Yan studied cell biology in a lab at the [[Institute of Biophysics, Chinese Academy of Sciences]] (CAS) until leaving for Germany to obtain a doctorate in 1989. She graduated with a medical doctor’s degree from [[Heidelberg University]] and later traveled to the United States to engage in post-doctoral research at the [[Memorial Sloan Kettering Cancer Center]] in [[New York City]]. Yan returned to China in 1997 and was selected for the Hundred Talents Program by CAS. Since then, Yan has focused on [[tumor]] research, working to discover new targets and advancing techniques for tumor diagnosis and [[Treatment of cancer|therapy]].

== Research summary ==
Yan Xiyun focused mainly on [[Cancer immunology|tumor immunology]] and nanozymes research. In 2007, Yan discovered [[Artificial enzyme#Nanozymes|nanozymes]] and proposed that nanoparticles possess [[Enzyme|enzymatic]] properties. Yan was the first to integrate the use of [[nanomaterials]] as enzymes mimic to advance tumor diagnosis and therapy. This compelling discovery of nanozyme shifted the initial idea that nanoparticles are [[Chemically inert|chemically inactive]], which unveiled many new applications for nanoparticles in the fields of [[medicine]], [[biotechnology]], [[Food industry|food production]], [[environmental protection]], and [[agriculture]].<ref name="springer" /> Today, nanozymes is seen as an emerging field that combines both [[nanotechnology]] and biotechnology. Tumor immunology research led her to discover [[CD146]], a melanoma cell adhesion molecule that is greatly expressed in tumor cells that leads to [[metastasis]].<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Luo |first1=Y |last2=Zheng |first2=C |last3=Zhang |first3=J |last4=Lu |first4=D |last5=Zhuang |first5=J |last6=Xing |first6=S |last7=Feng |first7=J |last8=Yang |first8=D |last9=Yan |first9=X |title=Recognition of CD146 as an ERM-binding protein offers novel mechanisms for melanoma cell migration |journal=Oncogene |year=2012 |volume=31 |issue=3 |pages=306–321 |doi=10.1038/onc.2011.244 |pmid=21725352 |s2cid=21579095 |doi-access= }}</ref> Yan and her team were able to determine the [[Ligand (biochemistry)|ligands]] of CD146, and develop treatments for liver, pancreatic, and colon cancer by creating therapeutic [[Humanized antibody|humanized antibodies]].<ref name="CAS">{{cite web |last1=Bai |first1=Chunli |title=Yan Xiyun |url=http://english.ibp.cas.cn/faculty/index_18316.html?json=http://www.ibp.cas.cn/sourcedb_ibp_cas/cn/ibpexport/EN_zgkxyys/202005/t20200519_5583027.json |website=Chinese Academy of Sciences |access-date=14 November 2020}}</ref> The discovery of nanozymes has won China's [[State Science and Technology Prizes|State Natural Science Award]].<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.ibp.cas.cn/sourcedb_ibp_cas/cn/ibpachiev/gjj/201305/t2013055_3840052.html |title=页面没有找到 |access-date=5 March 2023}}{{Dead-link|date=March 2023}}</ref> The work of Yan and her team has been recognized and published in [[Nature (journal)|Nature]], [[Blood (journal)|Blood]], [[Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences of the United States of America|PNAS]], and other journals.
